subject: Insurance
title: The Two-Year Contestability Period
description: A fast breakdown of The Two-Year Contestability Period for builders.

hook.text: If you die within two years of buying life insurance, the insurer can investigate whether you lied on the application.

buildup.text: The contestability period protects insurers from people who buy a policy knowing they're about to die.

discovery.text: If the insurer finds you hid a serious illness, they can deny the claim entirely.

twist.text: After two years, the policy becomes almost uncontestable. Even lies on the application can't void it in most states.

climax.text: The two-year rule balances fairness: insurers get time to verify, and policyholders get eventual certainty.

punchline.text: Lie on the application, die within two years. The insurer can deny everything.

quiz.question: What is the contestability period?
options: When you can cancel the policy
A window where insurers can investigate claims for fraud
The waiting period before coverage starts
